quarterly_data.quarter: Socionext results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 results briefing summary of Q&A (07-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing summary of Q&A, July 29, 2026) on its data center CPU product: management views data center CPU demand as solid and on an expanding trend, expects its customer's demand to exceed the company's initial forecast, and is working with the customer to secure foundry production capacity for the leading-edge process node. The company has new products scheduled to enter mass production in the second half of the fiscal year ending March 2027; the yield-improvement period and initial costs such as testing for new mass-production launches are factored into this year's forecast, and the company is applying lessons from the prior year's new automotive product launch, when cost improvements lagged and production volume rose beyond its assumptions, lifting the cost ratio more than expected. On design wins this fiscal year management gave no specifics but expects many inquiries about products for data centers and peripheral applications.

quarterly_data.quarter: Socionext results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 results briefing summary of Q&A (07-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing summary of Q&A) on the Q1 revenue shift: the supply-chain change was a partial revision of production and shipment operations for certain automotive products, to strengthen production capacity and optimise the supply structure; some product shipments shifted into Q2 because procedures tied to the change took longer than expected. Management says the shift is not directly related to any change in customer demand for the full fiscal year, and the change, made to improve production efficiency and optimise logistics, incurs no additional costs.

quarterly_data.quarter: Socionext results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 results briefing summary of Q&A (07-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 results briefing summary of Q&A) on R&D, NRE and margins: production of evaluation samples for new products entering mass production in the second half has increased, with those costs expected to be covered by NRE revenue, so NRE revenue is expected to rise year on year this fiscal year; R&D expenses are expected to stay at the Q1 level from Q2 onward as the company keeps investing in leading-edge fields. Some advance development (asked about chiplet and advanced packaging work) is needed for customers' product development, but most is upfront investment in leading-edge technologies to strengthen its Entire Design and Complete Service capabilities. Asked about the timing of NRE revenue, management says it does not indicate any particular delay in development: NRE per project has grown larger, so even a slight shift in tape-out timing moves it. Product gross margin fell year on year on a lower share of relatively high-margin products and higher reticle depreciation from the increase in advanced-technology products.
